mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the cost of capital decreases.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1% is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.3 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the market anticipates reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, the S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances, or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 5-day returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based demand slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in weaker corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The interaction of RSAFS and HOUST (both below their 1-year moving average) fails to predict negative 60-day returns: the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03, or the average 60-day return when both are below average is positive.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production growth (INDPRO) signals robust supply chain activity and corporate capacity utilization, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days during periods of strong supply growth.
failure_condition: When INDPRO > 105, the S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the cases, or the Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 20-day returns in the strong growth regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates robust household demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and generates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the market anticipates strong earnings.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for RSAFS as a predictor of 5-day S&P 500 returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 5-day return when RSAFS is above its 1-year average is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5 percentage points over one month signals rising inflation, prompting market concerns about monetary tightening and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in 1 month, the S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high unemployment (UNRATE) and weak job growth (PAYEMS) indicates a deteriorating labor market, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in reduced consumer spending and corporate hiring.
failure_condition: The interaction of UNRATE and PAYEMS (UNRATE > 6.0% and PAYEMS growth < 0.1% in 3 months) fails to predict negative 60-day returns: the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03, or the average 60-day return when both conditions are met is positive.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-rate environment (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%), strong industrial production growth (INDPRO) signals robust economic activity and corporate earnings potential, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and INDPRO > 105, the S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the cases, or the Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 20-day returns in the low-rate regime is below 0.03.
